facts.statement: Gladocephaloideus lived during the Early Cretaceous period in what is now western Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Gladocephaloideus is a genus of ctenochasmatid ctenochasmatoid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous period (early Aptian stage) of what is now western Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: The genus was named by Lü Junchang, Ji Qiang, Wei Xuefang, and Liu Yongqing in 2012.
facts.quote: It was named by Lü Junchang, Ji Qiang, Wei Xuefang and Liu Yongqing in 2012 and the type species is Gladocephaloideus jingangshanensis.

facts.statement: A second juvenile specimen was referred to the genus in 2016.
facts.quote: In 2016, a second specimen was referred, JPM 2014–004, a juvenile from the Jiufotang Formation.

facts.statement: Research indicated that the original holotype was actually a juvenile, not an adult.
facts.quote: Though the holotype was originally considered an adult, the new exemplar indicates that IG-CAGS-08-07 was a juvenile also.

facts.statement: Fossils date to about 121 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Jingangshan Bed of the Yixian Formation, dating to the early Aptian stage, about 121 million years ago.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence includes traces of hair-like pycnofibres.
facts.quote: Gladocephaloideus is known from a complete skull and partial postcranial skeleton including traces of hair-like pycnofibres.

facts.statement: The holotype skull measures 182 mm in length.
facts.quote: The skull of the holotype has a length of 182 mm.

facts.statement: The animal had an elongated snout.
The skull and lower jaws contained about fifty teeth in total.
facts.quote: The total number of teeth in the entire skull and lower jaws numbers about fifty.

facts.statement: The snout had a concave upper profile.
facts.quote: The snout has a concave upper profile.

facts.statement: Short hairs were visible at the back of the skull and neck vertebrae.
facts.quote: The pycnofibres in the holotype are visible as short hairs, pointing to the rear, at the back of the skull and the neck vertebrae.

facts.statement: The longest neck vertebra was 4.1 times longer than it was wide.
facts.quote: The longest neck vertebra is 4.1 times longer than wide.

facts.statement: The first phalanx of the wing finger was the longest bone and equal in length to the shinbone.
facts.quote: In the wing finger the first phalanx is the longest and equals the shinbone in length.

facts.statement: Later analysis placed the genus in the family Ctenochasmatidae as the sister species of Pterofiltrus.
facts.quote: In 2016 however, the new skeleton indicated that Gladiocephaloideus was in fact a member of the Ctenochasmatidae, as the sister species of Pterofiltrus.

facts.statement: The genus is now known to be part of Ctenochasmatidae and is a sister taxon to Pterofiltrus.
facts.quote: Gladocephaloideus se creyó el primer galodactílido hallado en Asia. Pero ahora se sabe que forma parte de Ctenochasmatidae y es un taxón hermano de Pterofiltrus.

facts.statement: The time range for the genus is estimated from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)
